title: "Metrics for Comparing Tabular Datasets"

This series develops metrics for comparing two tabular datasets, $X$ and $Y$,
that share a schema but may contain different values and different numbers of
rows. Neither table is assumed to be real or synthetic.

The introduction separates two views of the tables:

- the original $X,Y$ and their missingness masks $M_X,M_Y$; and
- complete metric-ready representations $\widetilde X,\widetilde Y$ produced
  by one shared transformation.

Later lessons will use these views to develop fidelity, missingness, utility,
and privacy metrics one at a time.

::: {.lesson-grid}
::: {.lesson-card}
### [0. Comparing $X$ and $Y$: Data Views and Notation](0.0-data-views-and-notation.ipynb)

Construct two small mixed-type tables, expose their missingness masks, and
follow every column into a shared complete representation.

**Prerequisites:** basic Python and introductory data-frame concepts.
:::
:::

## Series roadmap

### Complete metric-ready representations

- **Fidelity:** correlation-matrix difference and average empirical Hellinger
  distance.
- **Utility:** independent-holdout AUROC difference.
- **Privacy:** exact-match rate and distance-to-closest-record
  membership-inference AUC.

### Original incomplete tables

- **Missingness fidelity:** marginal missingness Hellinger distance, joint
  missingness Hellinger distance, and the missingness–value dependence gap.
